inputs.name: ticks

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

facts.text: The action space is Discrete(2): the integer action 0 or 1
Action 1 pushes the cart with +force_mag and any other action with -force_mag
The physics constants are gravity 9.8, masscart 1.0, masspole 0.1, length 0.5 (half the pole's length), force_mag 10.0 and tau 0.02 s between state updates, integrated with the euler scheme
The failure thresholds are 12 degrees for the pole angle and 2.4 for the cart position
The episode terminates when the cart position or the pole angle passes its threshold
The observation is [cart position, cart velocity, pole angle, pole angular velocity] with the bounds +-4.8, +-inf, about +-0.418 rad (24 degrees) and +-inf
The reward is +1 for every step, including the step that terminates the episode, and 0 after it
CartPoleEnv.step never truncates: the time limit is the TimeLimit wrapper that gymnasium.make adds
A reset draws the four state values uniformly from (-0.05, 0.05)
The reset option low or high replaces a bound of that draw (low must not exceed high)

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the initial state and the dynamics are deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; this package's fake draws initial states with Python's random.Random and upstream with numpy's generator, so a seed gives different trajectories on the two

gaps: rigid-body equations of motion of a cart and a pole on a frictionless track: no contacts, no friction and no actuator, sensor or noise model; the push is an ideal step force of fixed size
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms (tau 0.02 s) only
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

the fake backend re-implements the dynamics in pure Python floats and was not compared with the upstream environment (gymnasium was not importable where the gate ran): trajectories can differ from upstream's float32 observations and numpy random stream
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
